verified.analysis: The triage read the tape correctly but mis-assigned the lane: the overhang event it names — the Sept-1-2026 IPO lockup expiry — has already FIRED, six days ago, so what is being underwritten is a 4-8 week absorption forecast rather than a dated forward catalyst, and absorption clears no Bloom gate. The genuinely unfired item, the NRC final safety evaluation and construction permit for Long Mott, is real, well-dated (Nov-2026 target under the EO 14300 clock, draft SE done and environmental review closed with a FONSI) and has a named counterparty in Dow — but it fails G2 and G3 hard: Dow is on record that its final investment decision is not expected before 2028, so permit issuance commits no capital and produces no re-derivable figure to price against today's $17.71. The one honest positive is that nothing is harvested: at -23% from the IPO price and -52% off the high, this is an early-arc suppressed underlying with zero run-up, so it earns a WATCH — but per the score-the-equity-not-the-event rule the score caps at 4, and it should only escalate if a permit grant is paired with a dated, named, dollar-quantified Dow or third-party commitment rather than the 2028 FID placeholder.

verified.analysis: The event is verified, dated, unfired and not macro: a signed $35.00 all-cash merger, shareholder-approved 2026-04-30 (the triage's "97.4% May-26" date is off — the special meeting was April 30), with the single open condition being Israel's Special State Share consent and the FIMI "New ZIM" 16-vessel domestic carve-out, next tested at the 2026-09-09 eight-agency review and decided later by the Government Companies Authority. The triage's core claim — that the spread is "unresolved rather than priced" — does not survive: the 22.4% gross spread IS the market's handicap on this one consent, and the publicly reported information lean runs against approval (majority of the eight agencies expected to oppose per the 09-02 report, Knesset panel opposed in February, CEO Glickman sold 87% of his holdings below the offer per Mar-2026 reporting), so you would be paying a price implying ~55-60% approval into a base rate that reads worse. What saves it from a NONE is the unusually soft break case — standalone ZIM at record transpacific rates carries $2.46bn cash, no traditional debt, FY26 guided adj EBITDA $2.0-2.4bn against a $3.44bn cap, and an expected 2026 dividend, with at least one sell-side view arguing rejection is itself a positive catalyst. WATCH, not ACTIVE: buying two days ahead of a meeting whose expected headline is adverse is paying for the wrong side of the coin flip; the better seat is post-09-09 at $22-25, where you own cheap standalone ZIM plus a free option on the GCA overruling its ministries.
